tags.gist: Says the paper needs to draw the distinction between clinical validity and clinical utility more explicitly.
Frames its recommendations as extensions of existing tools, favouring risk-proportionate, postmarket-weighted oversight that keeps entry open for early-stage companies.
Urges importing the diagnostic distinction of analytic validity, clinical validity and clinical utility, mapping them to the paper's elements and confirmation.
Recommends sponsors test and label every device function separately for clinical validity and clinical utility, not one aggregate assessment.
Supports a risk-proportionate competency approach but warns fixed compliance cost must not become the main barrier to entry, entrenching incumbents.
Wants enforcement discretion and the existing CDS exclusion kept as the default for low-activity, non-directive, clinician-facing informational functions.
Would reserve prospective studies, mandatory third-party adjudication and extensive subgroup benchmarking for the highest-risk tier, not the middle.
Wants third-party accreditation, adjudication and master files strictly voluntary and non-gating, with shared or subsidized infrastructure for small entities.
Would make postmarket monitoring, not more premarket evidence, the primary way to manage residual uncertainty, calling continuous signal more accurate.
Says deployment-site capacity, not sponsor evidence, often limits safe use; wants minimum site capacity addressed, coordinated with CMS infrastructure.
Supports the two axes but wants evidentiary traceability to validated anchors as a third dimension or modifier, rewarding anchored functions with less burden.
Wants the consequences axis to carry deployment-context modifiers, since the same output matters more where no specialty coverage exists.
Recommends harmonizing the two-axis framework with the HHS high-impact AI classification rather than a separate taxonomy.
Suggests scope-anchored worker-extender certification, as CMS has integrated, to mitigate patient-facing risk without restricting patient information.
Endorses the two-stage frame as mirroring diagnostic validation pathways and asks guidance to say so explicitly.
Wants benchmarking alone, without mandatory clinical confirmation, to presumptively suffice across the lower and middle risk bands.
Wants elements labelled as validity or utility evidence, plus a new element checking that claim language matches evidence strength.
Wants a benchmarking element covering clinician usability and cognitive burden through human factors testing with front-line users.
Wants independently governed longitudinal clinical-genetic and outcomes databanks listed as a confirmation approach between retrospective and prospective.
Wants a rebuttable presumption against requiring prospective studies outside the highest-risk band, given their cost to early-stage firms.
Would make human-AI team performance the default comparator for worker-extender deployments, reserving device-alone for autonomous use.
Wants the comparator tied to the labelled configuration, with override behaviour and trust calibration measured over time.
Citing the vacated LDT rule, wants CLIA and CAP accreditation recognized as satisfying benchmarking and third-party elements for laboratory-embedded functions.
Suggests accredited laboratory infrastructure host sequestered datasets, cautions against any mandatory third-party gate, and wants subsidized shared infrastructure.
Wants the trade-off as the default outside the highest-risk band, as least burdensome, more protective for evolving devices, and cheaper.
Would extend the PCCP framework as the vehicle for prespecified monitoring plans with corrective action and auditability, excepting the highest-risk band.
Suggests accredited laboratory cadences, proficiency intervals and triggered reverification, as the model for periodic re-benchmarking.
Wants sample chart review by sponsor-independent practising clinicians as a standing element, using existing patient safety and peer-review bodies.
Wants compensation tied to device use treated as a monitoring risk category, disclosed in plans and weighed when reading performance signals.
Would anchor agentic oversight to the CDS exclusion's independent-review criterion: can a human genuinely review and reject a planned sequence.
Wants a bright-line test for meaningful independent review, including minimum information surfaced before irreversible actions, mindful of thin rural staffing.
Urges holding the device definition: orchestrating a non-device function with an agent should not by itself make it a device.
Encourages drawing on the layered validity and utility discipline of diagnostic testing, not only clinician credentialing.
Asks CDRH to match evidence and oversight to risk, rigorous where risk is high and light elsewhere, to sustain innovators.
